assertion_analysis.condition_to_fail: Dropping the sorted() over the test-file arguments in reckon/crew/promotion_records.py:590 makes the reversed-order command compare unequal, which is what the negative control demonstrates.

Removing the interpreter resolution in reckon/crew/promotion_records.py:578-583 leaves .venv/bin/python relative against the arm's absolute path, so the assertion refuses; the negative control demonstrates this.
Returning the words untouched from _leading_cd_tree at reckon/crew/promotion_records.py:506 keeps the cd words in the comparison, so the assertion refuses; the negative control demonstrates this.
Accepting a strict subset of the armed files (for example comparing only the first entry, or returning True from _arm_command_matches) lets the one-file command match and the assertion fails.
Filtering flag words out of the comparison at reckon/crew/promotion_records.py:594 makes the extra -x invisible, so the assertion fails.

findings.text: non-blocking: the fixture creates .venv/bin/python as a real file under a real .venv directory, so test_the_absolute_interpreter_of_the_runs_environment_matches passes on the join alone and never exercises the Path.resolve() that reckon/crew/promotion_records.py:527 performs. Every worktree in this repository symlinks .venv to the main checkout (this node's own worktree does), so a worker recording the main checkout's absolute interpreter is matched only because resolve() follows that symlink; a fixture making .venv a symlink would be the case that reddens if the resolve were dropped. Folded into a follow-up node is enough; the five done-when cases are otherwise covered.
